ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ABC=82^\circ$, $\angle C=58^\circ$, $BD\perp AC$ at $D$, $AE$ bisects $\angle CAB$, and $BD$ intersects $AE$ at point $F$. What is $\angle AFB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given: $\because \angle CAB = 180^\circ - \angle ABC - \angle C$,\\
and $\angle ABC = 82^\circ, \angle C = 58^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle CAB = 40^\circ$,\\
$\because$ AE bisects $\angle CAB$,\\
$\therefore \angle DAF = 20^\circ$,\\
$\because$ BD $\perp$ AC at D,\\
$\therefore \angle ADB = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle AFB = \angle ADB + \angle DAF = 90^\circ + 20^\circ = \boxed{110^\circ}$.
